newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit down sharply on covering, speculative sales.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit down sharply on covering, speculative sales.

text.p: The ringgit fell sharply against the dollar in late Asian trading on heavy speculative dollar buying and covering of short Singapore dollar positions, dealers said on Tuesday.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5145/55 to a dollar against its opening at 2.5015.
"We underestimated the ferociousness of the (dollar) buyers. They came in real strong and triggered a lot of stop-loss levels," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.
"Much of it was ringgit/Sing play. People were covering short Singapore dollar positions," he said.
Dealers said some funds bought huge amount of dollar, but quietly, taking advantage of the covering by speculators.
"Some banks were squaring their books before the month-end," said a senior dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said dollar/ringgit could go as high as 2.5180 to a dollar overnight, but some dealers said there was some profit-taking at the current levels.
The ringgit sales were triggered by a sharp drop in currency swaps and Malaysian interbank rates in the last two days.
"The swaps are back to normal and so are the interbank rates," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.

He said the markets had calmed down after the interest rate rises caused by an aggressive central bank intervention to prevent the ringgit's fall two weeks ago. The central bank was said to have sold around $1 billion.
The intervention drained liquidity from the system, causing the market to be short, and interbank rates to rise to unusually high levels, dealers said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were mixed as the selling triggered by interest rate falls were countered by covering of positions, futures dealers said.
At the close, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) contract for June 1997 was unchanged at 92.49, or an implied yield of 7.51 percent.
September 1997 contract was down one point at 92.60, or 7.40 percent and December was down two at 92.60, or 7.40 percent.
